title: Taming Silent Failures: A Framework for Verifiable AI Reliability
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of silent failures in AI-enabled safety-critical systems: cases where a model produces confident but incorrect outputs without an explicit crash, error, or warning. The authors argue that conventional pre-deployment testing and white-box verification are insufficient for complex deep neural networks operating in open-world conditions, especially under distribution shift, sensor faults, occlusion, and other environmental stressors.

To address this, the paper proposes the Formal Assurance and Monitoring Environment (FAME), a two-phase framework that combines offline formal specification and synthesis with online runtime monitoring and mitigation. Safety requirements are expressed in Signal Temporal Logic and converted into lightweight monitors that observe AI inputs and outputs at runtime, detect violations, and trigger fail-safe, fail-operational, or fail-degraded responses. The framework also includes a feedback loop that logs violations for retraining and specification refinement.

The paper’s empirical demonstration uses a YOLOv4 pedestrian-detection system in the CARLA simulator for an autonomous driving perception task. Across nominal and challenging driving scenarios, the authors report that the monitor detected most silent failures while producing no false positives in nominal conditions. The main conclusion is that verifiable runtime assurance can provide a practical safety net around opaque AI components, and that this approach may support certification-oriented safety processes such as ISO 26262 and ISO/PAS 8800. The paper is not an education study and does not involve K-12 learners or teachers.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a framework and proof-of-concept engineering paper, not a K-12 educational intervention study. It reports a single simulated autonomous-vehicle case study rather than a rigorous educational evaluation, so it does not meet criteria for educational evidence quality tiers beyond descriptive/technical demonstration.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no direct educational outcome or K-12 impact reported. The paper’s results concern detection of silent failures in a simulated perception system, not learner achievement, engagement, or institutional outcomes in education.

interventions.use_case: runtime assurance / formal verification framework for monitoring AI-powered perception outputs, synthesizing safety monitors from STL specifications to detect silent failures, misinformation-like wrong outputs, and overreliance risks in safety-critical systems
